reasoning: The document extract contains only one theme, marked 'not core', with just two sentences: 'It will be reviewed' and a mention of a review date of 10/2021. There is no indication of what success measures will be used, no explanation of plans to test the policy before implementation, no description of outcomes to be measured, and no detail on how any evaluation will be conducted or what will happen to its results. The phrase 'it will be reviewed' is a bare statement of intent to revisit the policy at some point, but it gives no sense of criteria, methodology, or publication plans, so it cannot even support a level 1 claim of 'some indication of success measures'. Since no theme in this extract is marked core, the section as a whole must be scored on the thin evidence available, which is essentially nil for this aspect of the argument. The strongest counter-example to a score of 0 would be if the review date itself implied an evaluation timetable, but a date alone without any description of what will be evaluated or how does not meet even the lowest bar for 'indication of success measures'. To reach level 1, the document would need to state at least one measurable outcome or success indicator; to reach level 2 it would need a testing or evaluation plan, or a justification for omitting one.
